If you are looking to attach one, follow this quick guide to hand-sew it securely: 
🧵 How to Sew a Two-Hole Button
  1. Prepare your thread: Cut about 2 feet of thread. Pass it through your needle and double it up, tying a strong knot at the long end.

jsaction="rcuQ6b:&QUOsBe_v4|npT2md" jscontroller="XqmSxe#JjQTXe" data-sfc-root="ep" data-epip="" data-wiz-uids="QUOsBe_v8,QUOsBe_va,QUOsBe_vb" data-complete="true" data-sfc-inited="2"> 
  • Anchor the fabric: Mark where you want the button to go. Poke your needle through from the back side of the fabric to the front so the knot stays hidden on the back. 
  • Stitch the button: Push the needle up through the first hole of the button, then send it straight down through the second hole and back through the fabric.

"true"> 
  • Leave room for the fabric (The Shank): Place a toothpick or a thick needle under the button while you stitch. This creates a small gap so your garment can glide under the button easily when fastened.

How to Sew a Two-hole Button By Hand

items.text:
A two-hole button (also known as a flat or pass-through button) is a classic fastener attached to clothing or craft projects by sewing thread up through one hole and down through the other. 
Aboderie
 +1
If you are looking to attach one, follow this quick guide to hand-sew it securely:
🧵 How to Sew a Two-Hole Button
Prepare your thread: Cut about 2 feet of thread. Pass it through your needle and double it up, tying a strong knot at the long end. 
YouTube
·Lauren Bloom
 +2
Anchor the fabric: Mark where you want the button to go. Poke your needle through from the back side of the fabric to the front so the knot stays hidden on the back. 
YouTube
·Drink and Sew Things
 +2
Stitch the button: Push the needle up through the first hole of the button, then send it straight down through the second hole and back through the fabric. 
YouTube
·Bernadette Banner
 +1
Leave room for the fabric (The Shank): Place a toothpick or a thick needle under the button while you stitch. This creates a small gap so your garment can glide under the button easily when fastened. 
Instagram
·Mset Fashion Design
 +1
Repeat: Repeat this up-and-down process 5 to 7 times to make sure it is strong. 
YouTube
·Makewell with Miss Markwell
 +1
Wrap and knot: Bring your needle to the front underneath the button. Remove your toothpick and wrap your thread tightly around the exposed stitches 5 or 6 times to create a sturdy "shank". Push the needle back to the wrong side of the fabric, tie a double knot, and snip the excess thread. 
YouTube
·Lauren Bloom
